未來新task（不是現有能力）：

## V01 — correctness/property suite

固定合成賬戶 A `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001`、B `...0002`，BigDecimal兩位，round `1.005→1.01`。餘額初始化由fixtureload完成，不在timed/critical section強行createaccount。

| case | assertion | task |
|---|---|---|
| rejectednegative/zero/out-of-range | 無balance/version/queuedwork變化 | T01/T02 |
| withdrawal concurrentinsufficient | 正確該次結果，不從其他writer版本猜成功 | T02 |
| receivercancels transfer100/0→10 | 最終100/0，總量100，無單腿遺留 | T07 |
| fulladmission + alloverflowunavailable | 立即拒絕，無mutation或成功event | T03 |
| coldexistingbalance100 | no syncI/O；miss不persist0；asyncready後100 | T04 |
| multipleasync loads sameUUID | 一個loader，pendingmutation不被stalesnapshot蓋掉 | T04 |
| confirmedRedis90/v7 then concurrent v8 | 同receipt90/7進wire和SQL，不配90/8 | T05 |
| SQL v41 followed delayedv40 | row不regress（僅新writer）；同v不同moneyconflict | T05 |
| Lua wrongreceiver/versiontype/overflow | 第一次mutation前reject；餘額不變 | T06 |
| alreadyexecuted,response lost | 去重確認或quarantine，不能第二次ADD | T06 |
| markerabsent + SENT_UNKNOWN | 無blind retry，即使未滿TTL | T06/T08 |
| two-nodecached100 eachwithdraw80 | 明確authorityreject、pendingrebuild/unavailable，不能假globalfinal | T07 |
| partialpairSQL | transactionrollback/整對stale拒絕；不能onlyoneleg持久化 | T07 |
| recoveryread/crash/ack/compact | 原記錄不先clear，成功後checkpoint | T08 |
| pendingwriteeviction/logout | 不丟事件或confirmedbase/pendingowner | T03/T15 |
| pluginAPIattribution/hooks | 正確name，一次pre/post/completion；cancel無資金變化 | T02/T11 |
| restartrequired reload | snapshot/owner均不halfapply | T09 |
| schemaDDLfailed | metadata不advance；newerschema不隱式變更 | T09 |
| equal/older remote | noappliedupdate/nooverwrite；unknownenum可讀 | T10 |
| CMIclock/retirement | freshness在ownercallback再次判定、noecho | T13 |
| shutdownqueueemptyretryfull | drain/recordpending、storage仍live | T15 |

所有concurrencyfixture采用latches/barriers/manualexecutor，禁止靠sleep通過率證明正確。隨機propertytests固定seed並記錄失敗seed；fakecontract與realbackends相同。

## V02 — protocol／數據fixtures

保存actual1.3.2 codec/source讀取後的合成goldens：optionalomitted、primitiveamount0.0、unknownevent/field、UUIDbad、missingfield、非finite金額、long>2^53、CMIeventtype、sourceServer/messageIdecho、reorder/duplicate。Java讀long不得經JS浮點roundtrip。

FreezeLua KEY/ARGV/return/errorcontract，特別set鍵順序是version/balance，add是balance/version。原數值double與截斷結果不能被提取順手改成decimalstring。腳本修覆另保存before/afterexpectation。

SQL fixtures必須分別：

- shared PostgreSQL/MySQL實際 `players.player_uuid`、DECIMAL20,2、BIGINT與schema table。
- MariaDB通過既有mysqlconnection配置真實啟動，不能假設有獨立正式mode。
- LOCAL SQLite `player_balances`/`transactions` 的REAL/int既有格式與同路徑。
- audit id='audit'/11、main id='1'/1、baltop、Shadow；disabledmodule不創建它的schema。
- configschema12、messages/alias、unknownoperator鍵（值都是無secret合成值）。

Each report contains six startup/runtime Syncmoney pins across baseline, candidate, and rollback stages on both node identities; the candidate Vault API consumer and write receipts passed. SQL and Redis snapshots agree at every observed stage: `1000.00/v1, 520.00/v1` before upgrade; `1337.25/v2, 765.50/v2` after the first candidate node; and `1444.25/v3, 820.50/v3` after the second candidate node and both 1.3.2 rollback reads. Each report has six healthy normal server stops and two six-frame candidate recovery journals; both journals were byte-identical at rollback, passed format/checksum validation, and had zero pending records. Each report also records all four verified backend stops at exactly `preupgrade-backup` and `final-cleanup`: Redis `SHUTDOWN SAVE` exit 0 with process exit 0; PostgreSQL running status exit 0 with PID marker, `pg_ctl stop` exit 0, and exact stopped status exit 3. Isolated Gradle `--stop` exited 0 with no matching daemon remaining.

The cleanup gate now fails closed if a ready Redis process exits before the requested `SHUTDOWN SAVE`; it only records success after command and process exit are verified. PostgreSQL running status requires exit 0 and a PID marker; stopped status requires exit 3 and the exact `pg_ctl: no server running` text. Unknown PostgreSQL status triggers a bounded stop against the isolated data directory, but the run remains failed even if the subsequent stop is verified. A PASS additionally requires one successful Redis and PostgreSQL observation at each of the two required stages, both started flags cleared, and no `cleanupFailure`. The runner also gates exact stop-stage coverage per node and the deployed Syncmoney JAR SHA-256 on every baseline/candidate/rollback start. The 16-case cleanup test and 29-case T21 validation test include negative cases for the rejected states and mismatched pins.

**Verification:** `pwsh -NoProfile -File build/reports/foundation/T21-sync-upgrade/verify-corrected-platform-sync-reports.ps1` exited 0 and reported all seven retained reports final=True for runtime identity, lifecycle, plugin pins, backend shutdown coverage, SQL/Redis parity, recovery journals, Gradle cleanup, and clean exit. The independent current-runner source review found no actionable findings. At this checkpoint the independent evidence review was pending. A later independent audit/review covers the six user-pinned endpoint reports only; it does not cover historical Paper `26.3#175`, which remains NOT independently reviewed and excluded from acceptance. The supplemental current-stable Paper `26.3#178` report is recorded separately below.

**Limits / disposition:** These are sequential, bounded two-node SYNC cases, not fleet-wide producer fencing or simultaneous mixed-version writes. No full queue/retry/in-flight/audit counters are exposed by this runtime; those values remain NOT EXPOSED / NOT TESTED. The reports do not establish hard-crash/power-loss recovery, all mode/backend/dialect/failure combinations, Folia/Canvas entity-scheduler safety, or licensed CMI behavior. **Runner discovery and retry disposition:** Redis `8.10.1` omits `aof_last_load_status` from `INFO persistence`. The harness therefore requires AOF enabled, rejects a present status other than `ok`, and always verifies exact balance/version readback after restart; absence of this field is not treated as a Redis durability claim. Six earlier Paper `1.21.6#48` attempts failed before the accepted final run due to harness setup/observation issues: transient listener ownership lookup, command result shape, candidate artifact resolution, a success marker absent during polling but present in the saved server log, reading an incremental AOF while Redis still held it open, and assuming `aof_last_load_status` exists. The file-hash check now occurs after verified graceful Redis shutdown. Final harness checks passed PowerShell parsing, AOF status predicate 5/5, and `node --test tools/plugdev/prepare.test.mjs` 7/7; two final minimum-Paper runs passed. Independent shutdown/lifecycle review and targeted AOF-status review found no actionable remaining issue. Normal shutdown left an internal `recovery-v1.jsonl` spool (3,409 bytes; four RECORD and two ACK frames); independent frame folding found zero pending records. This is an observation of the normal-drain path, not proof of hard-crash durability, power-loss recovery, or downgrade safety. M06 does not establish scheduler behavior for Folia/Canvas or complete V03 compatibility.

### M10 offline-audit physical-line boundary repair (2026-10-14)

A second source-pin review found a P2 evidence-audit defect: in .NET regular expressions, `\s` includes CR and LF. Because each marker was matched against the full server-log text, field fragments on adjacent physical lines could be combined into an apparent deposit receipt or stale-memory snapshot. This finding concerns the provenance audit only; it does not invalidate or change the six runtime observations.

Both marker patterns now use `[ \t]+` between fields, allowing horizontal separators while preventing a match from crossing a physical line. ### T21 SQL pool cleanup when `DatabaseManager` schema initialization fails (2026-10-17)

**Result: `PASS_BOUNDED_E1` for the constructor-owned Hikari pool failure path.** `StorageManager.initialize()` assigns `databaseManager` only after `new DatabaseManager(plugin, config)` returns. ## B00 — Benchmark profiles與command合同

As of 2026-10-09, T19 implements these Gradle tasks and runner CLI in `:syncmoney-benchmarks`; use the commands below only when the required hash-bound baseline pilot and endpoint configuration are available.

loadTest requires a hash-bound 1.3.2 Redis/SQL macro-pilot manifest; the synthetic facade acceptance rate from runBaselineComparison is explicitly invalid for load calibration. The baseline JAR is rebuilt with Java 21, while both macro pilot and current measurement must run on Java 25. Keep Redis/SQL endpoint credentials in the named environment variables and out of commands/reports.

```powershell
.\gradlew.bat :syncmoney-benchmarks:benchmarkJar
java -jar syncmoney-benchmarks/build/libs/SyncmoneyBenchmarks.jar -wi 5 -i 10 -w 1s -r 1s -f 3 -prof gc -jvmArgsAppend '-XX:+UseSerialGC -Dnet.bytebuddy.experimental=true -Xmx1g' -rf json -rff build/reports/benchmarks/jmh-1.4.0.json
.\gradlew.bat :syncmoney-benchmarks:runBaselineComparison '-PbaselineCheckout=C:/absolute/disposable/verified-1.3.2'
.\gradlew.bat :syncmoney-benchmarks:loadTest -Pprofile=syncmoney-benchmarks/profiles/redis-sql-open-loop.json '-PbaselineCheckout=C:/absolute/disposable/verified-1.3.2' '-PbaselinePilot=C:/absolute/evidence/verified-1.3.2-redis-sql-macro-pilot.json'
```

JMH runner使用明確annotationprocessor/version鎖定，獨立fork，不在IDE跑。JMHparams：accountcount1/1000/10000，producer1/2/8，queuecapacitylegacy50000與小capacity壓力case，hotkey集中與均勻。通過@Setup預熱/初始化/重置，各runpostcondition檢查資金與版本，不在measuredoperation準備環境。

| benchmark | variant | 輸出 |
|---|---|---|
| balance read | warmed、cold/unready異步schedule separate | ns/op、bytes/op、cachedstatus |
| deposit/withdraw/set | success、reject、cancel、hotcontention | ops/s、sampletime、alloc、outcomerate |
| transfer | localpair、Redisconfirmedasync分開 | acceptance/receiptlatency、conservation |
| queue | reserve/commit/dequeue、full、多producer | offered/accepted/reject、tail、CPU、GC |
| serialization | legacyminimal/full/CMI/badJSON | bytes/op、encode/decode latency、wireequivalence |
| messageprocess | newer/equal/older/duplicate/burst | apply/rejectrate、alloc、lag |
| batchpersistence | batch1/50/200/500 + maxwait1/5/20ms | rows/s、commitlatency、oldestage、rollback |
| macro pipeline | Redis/SQL healthy/slow/down/reconnect | p50/95/99/99.9、reject、persisted、backlogrepair |

主要paired profile固定JDK25/heap/GC、hardwareCPU/RAM/OS、flags、CPU affinity/power settings、Redis/SQL版本與network；1.3.2使用原Java21編譯artifact在Java25執行，1.4.0使用Java25編譯artifact，兩者測量JVM相同。另跑1.3.2/Java21作歷史profile、1.3.2/Java25作JVM影響profile；不可把Java21舊結果直接與Java25新結果混成架構收益。若舊artifact無法於Java25執行，標paired比較BLOCKED，先處理baseline harness相容且保留舊語義，不虛構數值。交錯跑避免溫度/CPU噪聲；3 forks不是p99.9充分樣本保證。Java25.0.4 Windows host上的paired JMH先後在G1與ParallelGC profile出現native process crash；根因未知。同一失敗列各在ParallelGC與SerialGC下各成功跑完一次，不足以判定根因；依ADR-17，paired及current-only JMH改用**僅限benchmark量測的SerialGC profile**，並保留ADR-08全部correctness/sample gates。Macro pilot與open-loop仍維持ParallelGC profile：r2 macro pilot曾通過，open-loop尚未執行；它們是分開的Redis/SQL runner，不作JMH stability的替代證據。這些GC選擇不改Syncmoney runtime GC，也不宣稱HotSpot根因已知。

所有macro-pilot、open-loop及JMH測量fork固定最大heap為1 GiB，並使用ByteBuddy flag。Paired與current-only JMH使用SerialGC；macro pilot與open-loop使用ParallelGC。每次paired comparison的baseline/candidate必須共用相同JDK、GC、heap與JVM flags，不得混算不同profile。Macro pilot保留response/receipt/durable/accepted-time樣本直到報告生成，因此每次measurement最多允許1,000,000個offered樣本；profile要求更高minimum時必須在連接Redis/SQL前拒絕。此上限仍高於100,000個p99.9最低樣本門檻10倍；超限時measurement失敗，不截斷樣本或輸出部分valid報告。

Macroopenloop到達率用baseline可持續acceptedrate的25/50/75/100/125%，不是手寫漂亮ops數；每檔120秒warm+300秒measurement起始、≥100000samples，實際profile由pilot確認。記錄**scheduledarrival到response**（含schedlag），另記錄accept到confirmedreceipt/durablecommit；reject也是response樣本。HDR原始/expectedintervalcorrected分開標，closedloop用於diagnostic不能替代openloop。

Result JSON fields：runId、sourceSHA、baselineSHA、artifactSHA256、profileId、JDK/OS/hardware/deps、flags、dataset、duration/sampleCount、offered/accepted/rejected/persisted、responseHistogram、receiptHistogram、durableHistogram、allocationBytesPerOp、GC、queueMax/oldestAge、ambiguous/quarantine、moneyInvariantFailures、versionConflicts、notes。含counts不足時標 p99.9不可靠，不能造confidenceinterval。

**Performance regression/review gates（非hard money gate）：** matched p99≤baseline110%、allocation/op≤110%、throughput≥90%；p99.9結合confidence/samplecount。超過須profile/cost分析與maintainer documented exception，correctness修復的合理成本可接受；不靜默改threshold／刪rejected samples。**Hard blockers：** money invariant violation、confirmed loss/corruption、contract禁止的incorrect success、unsafe unbounded pipeline、禁止hotpath network/SQL/filesystem blocking。這些即使性能很好仍FAIL，不能performance exception。Cold behavior差異不得冒充收益。

**Agrona合並條件：** 同contract/全部faultsuite、無unboundedspin/更高idleCPU，allocation或tail有可重覆收益且maintainerreview覆雜度；不滿足保留JDKqueue。Batchcoalescing只能safeabsoluteSQLsnapshot，不能丟audit或ADDrequest identity、不能穿SET/transferbarrier。

### T19 JMH dependency research

Checked 2026-10-09 against first-party JMH/OpenJDK metadata and official Gradle documentation:

- **Version:** JMH `1.37` is the newest version tag observed in the [official JMH tags](https://github.com/openjdk/jmh/tags) (tag commit `2effa2c8310e1d3ad03c8ee02024edca9252b46a`). Maven Central metadata independently reports `latest` and `release` as `1.37` for both [`jmh-core`](https://repo.maven.apache.org/maven2/org/openjdk/jmh/jmh-core/maven-metadata.xml) and [`jmh-generator-annprocess`](https://repo.maven.apache.org/maven2/org/openjdk/jmh/jmh-generator-annprocess/maven-metadata.xml).
- **Version alignment / processor:** The [JMH 1.37 benchmark archetype POM](https://github.com/openjdk/jmh/blob/1.37/jmh-archetypes/jmh-java-benchmark-archetype/src/main/resources/archetype-resources/pom.xml) pins both artifacts to the same `${jmh.version}`; the tagged [annotation-processor module POM](https://github.com/openjdk/jmh/blob/1.37/jmh-generator-annprocess/pom.xml) inherits parent version `1.37` and depends on `jmh-core` at `${project.version}`. JMH's [README](https://github.com/openjdk/jmh/blob/1.37/README.md) says annotation/bytecode processing is needed to generate benchmark code and that `jmh-core` alone is insufficient; it recommends a standalone benchmark project and describes a separate subproject as customary for large projects.
- **Narrow dependency arrangement:** use the existing `:syncmoney-benchmarks` subproject without a JMH Gradle plugin; define one fixed `jmhVersion = "1.37"`, put `org.openjdk.jmh:jmh-core:$jmhVersion` on that project's implementation/runtime path, and explicitly put `org.openjdk.jmh:jmh-generator-annprocess:$jmhVersion` on its `annotationProcessor` path. Keep both out of every production module and production artifact; only the isolated benchmark runner may package JMH runtime dependencies.
- **Java 25 compatibility:** first-party JMH 1.37 CI still does not claim Java 25 support, but the T19 local compile/build and Java 25 runner smoke now pass. The exact observed scope and remaining full-measurement limitations are recorded under Executed evidence — T19 below.

HDR Histogram dependency research checked 2026-10-09 against first-party HdrHistogram tags and Maven Central metadata: `org.hdrhistogram:HdrHistogram:2.2.2` is the latest observed release. Its tagged POM targets Java 8 bytecode. Its official CI stops at Java 21, so Java 25 compatibility is UNKNOWN until the isolated T19 runner compiles and exercises the histogram dependency. Keep it benchmark-only; no production module or plugin artifact may depend on it. Sources: https://github.com/HdrHistogram/HdrHistogram/tags, https://repo.maven.apache.org/maven2/org/hdrhistogram/HdrHistogram/maven-metadata.xml, https://github.com/HdrHistogram/HdrHistogram/blob/HdrHistogram-2.2.2/pom.xml, https://github.com/HdrHistogram/HdrHistogram/blob/HdrHistogram-2.2.2/.github/workflows/maven.yml.

## M00 — Upgrade engineering conditions

Supported upgrade：Existing Syncmoney1.3.2 persisted balance/config/SQL/Redis可原地升1.4而不reset，前提Paper≥1.21.6、Java≥25與健康配置/依賴。Paper≤1.21.5或Java≤24先升platform/runtime，不屬直接runtime guarantee；無需保留舊platform support。另確認唯一server-name、mode、backup/drain、無ambiguous recovery；不自動修壞moneykey或換authority。

**2026-10-05 T02 outage behavior / migration note:** in shared/synchronized modes, a known Redis-degraded state rejects new deposit, withdraw, and SET requests before memory mutation, transaction events, or queue admission. LOCAL remains on its SQLite path. Work accepted before the outage stays in the existing in-process write/retry tracking and resumes against Redis after recovery; SQL is not promoted to shared authority. This narrows the 1.3.2 degraded DB-fallback behavior. No config, schema, or Redis wire change is made; `pay.allow-in-degraded` retains its existing transfer-only meaning and default. This is E1 fixture evidence only: pending work is not hard-crash durable, and shutdown/restart recovery remains outside T02 (E08 stays INCONCLUSIVE/P0-CANDIDATE and non-mandatory).

### M01 — 備份與維護窗口

- [ ] 先確認Java≥25、Paper≥1.21.6 actual service/container啟動與dependencies；舊JVM/server先升環境，保留完整回復配置，不reset SQL/Redis/balances。原1.3.2 JAR在新環境若不支援，採離線合成fixture資料遷入supported環境驗證，不要求1.4維護舊platform。
- [ ] 記錄source/JARsha、Java/server/deps、configschema、SQLmain/auditschema、Redis版本與topology；不輸出secret。
- [ ] 全node關閉經濟producer／third-party自動reward與管理員寫入，確認API已unregister/healthquiescing。
- [ ] drain queue、inflight、retry、DB與audit至zero或穩定可確認pending；pending無法確認則停止upgrade。
- [ ] 正常stop所有nodes，備份config/messages/aliases、SQL、LOCALSQLite及WAL/SHM（優先SQLitebackupAPI或完全關閉後拷貝）、RedisRDB/AOF、overflow/recovery；保存preupgradehash。

### M02 — 更新與canary

- [ ] 每台plugins僅一份 `Syncmoney-1.4.0.jar`，主類/datafolder不變；PAPIexpansion仍可舊版起步驗證。
- [ ] 先canary，關閉producer；確認startup/schema/key/config保留，API/Vaultready、optionaldisabled符合，webunsafe例外明確。
- [ ] 使用**disposable acceptance賬戶**執行read/write驗證（productioncanary測試須當時批準小範圍寫入），正確handler/codec與receipt；不拿真用戶餘額做破壞性fault。
- [ ] 其餘nodes升級，各節點ready且無mixedoldwriter後恢覆producer。記錄升級前後總量、版本與reconcile差異；健康OK不等於數據驗收自動通過。

### M03 — 正常降級

- [ ] 1.4.0 JAR不能在Java21載入。plugin降回1.3.2可先保留已驗證的Java25；若另需降JVM，須配回支援Java21的server與dependencies，26.2新server不可假定能降回Java21。
- [ ] 再quiesce所有nodes並drain，保存**當前最新數據**與現有recovery紀錄（若採newspool也保存）。
- [ ] 若ADR-07核準new `recovery-v1.jsonl`，其pending/ambiguous必須已解決，不能給舊reader忽略後說rollback成功。
- [ ] 換回verified1.3.2JAR，保留當前compatibleSQL/Redis/SQLite/config數據；不清Redis、不把version歸零。
- [ ] 讀取upgrade期間新交易並驗證仍在；舊writer重新引入已知stale寫入限制，downgrade說明恢覆該限制。
- [ ] 舊backup只用於另行批準的災難恢覆；restore會丟升級後合法交易，不能算seamlessrollback。

沒有destructiveDDL或incompatiblewire並不自動證明rollback，newrecovery與behavior也要驗收。

## M04–M12 — 數據／mixed-version矩陣

| ID | old→new/new→old scenarios | expected/releasepolicy |
|---|---|---|
| M04 | LOCALsyntheticSQLitewithhistoricaltransactions | schema/path/REAL值可讀、normaldrain兩方向 |
| M05 | SYNCPostgreSQL/MySQL/MariaDB | player_uuid與schemaids不變、新guardwrites不會回退 |
| M06 | LOCAL_REDIS/AOFrestart | legacykey/result相容，noSQLresource；實際Redisdurability依配置 |
| M07 | CMIold/newwireclockskew | 明確freshness/collisionlimitations，licensedscenario |
| M08 | config12/customkeys/oldschemafailedbackup | preserve/idempotent/fail原檔、reload不halfapply |
| M09 | old→new、新→oldJSON/unknownfield/CMIlong | codec互通，duplicate/stale無apply |
| M10 | disconnect/reconnect/duplicate/receivedelayed | at-most-once丟訊後可reconcile，noecho |
| M11 | oldSQLv40在newv41之後 | **預期能展示legacyrace，不能宣稱live-mixed強一致** |
| M12 | old/newnodes live sameaccountwrites/transfer/failures | 默認unsupported；結果記錄，無matrix/ADR不擴展stable承諾 |

Drop-in artifact replacement、data compatibility、quiesced rolling、zero-downtime/live writes分開報告（定義04§15）；零停機不是既有承諾。ProposedCapability不證明未知peer真實行為，oldpeer永遠按legacy處理。

## Report模板／release gates

| 字段 | 內容 |
|---|---|
| Status | PASS / FAIL / BLOCKED / NOT_RUN（不混用） |
| Artifacts | actualSHA/version/buildsettings |
| Runtime | exactserver/JDK/optionaldependency/storageversions |
| Case | test/scenario/profile、input、faultpoint |
| Expected/Observed | 各自獨立，附assertion/record |
| Triage / priority | 08 finding ID、CONFIRMED/DISPROVED/INCONCLUSIVE/DEFERRED、issue priority與review；不與測試PASS/FAIL混用 |
| Remainingrisk | coldVaulttradeoff、hardcrashwindow、mixedwriters、CMIclock等 |
| Evidence | ignoredreport路徑與redactedsummary；不提交secrets/logs |

Alpha/Beta/Stable規則依04§24。沒有realFolia/CMI/network證據不可用unit/build作為替代；明確blocking或縮窄支持聲明需maintainerreview。

## Acceptance routing

V03正式support與歷史研究分開。所有CONFIRMED [P0]需修復／regression關閉；[P0-CANDIDATE]按08四種triage及review處理，未再現不自動成blocker；ADR-03/04/06/07在相關product/implementation/freeze前核準。Read-only SDK absence/shutdown/error contract、兩份descriptor api-version1.21.6、Paper1.21.6實際載入及最新supported Paper state upgrade不可被performance例外豁免。
public mutation/idempotency、Aeron transport與Agrona primitives、full engine redesign不是本matrix的隱含前置。Report增加priority與ADR approval／performance exception欄，NOT_RUN不算PASS。

CodeQL review dispositions (independent review completed 2026-10-05):

The first Java/Kotlin CodeQL database capture did not capture source through the Gradle daemon. The rerun used Gradle `--no-daemon --rerun-tasks`, then completed source capture and analysis successfully (243/243 Java files). The JavaScript/TypeScript scan used a clean mirror of tracked plus non-ignored current source and captured 91/91 JS/TS files and 3/3 GitHub Actions files. Final SARIF invocation status is successful for both runs. The first failed capture is not counted as a passed scan; no findings were suppressed.

- `java/toctou-race-condition`, `PlayerTransactionGuard.java:142`, severity 7.7; SARIF related locations are :118 and :137. The message links state use at :142 to a previous call at :137. Source shows separate synchronized `incrementTransactionsPerSecond()` and `incrementTransactionsPerMinute(amount)` methods updating distinct counters; no invariant requiring atomicity across the pair was identified. Independent review disposition: **likely false positive for an unsafe shared-state race**, based on source analysis. Runtime quota stress was NOT RUN, so no general rate-limit coverage claim is made.
- Separate independent-review observation: `TransferOrchestrator` calls receiver `deposit` before `checkAndLockReceiverForTransfer`. **INCONCLUSIVE; not reproduced; not a CodeQL alert.** A withdrawal may race after the deposit returns and before the receiver lock is applied; no funds-invariant violation is established. T01 owns a barrier-controlled interleaving after receiver deposit commit and before lock apply; record caller/mode/observed result and assess the documented guard contract.
- Six `js/empty-password-in-configuration-file` alerts at `src/main/resources/config.yml:33, 44, 398, 461, 470, 485`: **conditional operator-configuration risks.** They map to optional Redis, database, migration-CMI, and Shadow Sync SQL password fields. Tracked defaults use localhost for Redis/database/migration CMI; Shadow Sync selects SQLite, leaving its SQL variants dormant. The plugin passes configured values through and does not require a nonempty password. Deployments selecting remote services must supply credentials and protect endpoints. Credential values were not inspected or printed. Independent review accepted this bounded disposition; it is not a claim that remote deployments are secure by default.
- Two `js/missing-origin-check` alerts at line 23 in the generated and source MSW worker assets: **production false positives under the current boundary.** `syncmoney-web/src/main.ts` starts MSW only when `import.meta.env.DEV` is true. Development-server exposure remains the relevant condition.
- Independent T00A review found no remaining CodeQL gate blocker. It also found a P2 preview-label mismatch: CI uses repository variable `NEXT_VERSION`, currently documented as `1.3.3`, while the local candidate build used `1.4.0-alpha.1`. This does not change T00A's local artifact or stable metadata; defer target preview-line selection to T22 before preview release work.

Previously open: wrapper/checksum, Java 25 build/tests/coverage, classfile 69/consumer, dependency compatibility, minimum runtime smoke, CodeQL execution and independent review are now complete. CodeQL has reviewed findings; exit 0 does not mean zero findings. Latest Paper/Folia/Canvas and full state-upgrade coverage remain assigned to T21/V03.

Decision recorded from the user on 2026-10-05: when `MigrationLock` is active, reject all external writes, including `ADMIN_SET` and `COMMAND_ADMIN`; permit exactly the migration worker's own one-shot `ADMIN_SET`. The permit is consumed at `TransactionWriter.setBalance` entry so synchronous callbacks cannot reuse it. `MigrationTask` now treats null/negative rejected results as player migration failure before backup checkpoint, SQL, or optional Redis effects.

CMI source quiescence is resolved under ADR-11. Before snapshot, Syncmoney requires configured CMI economy command/module auto-disable, writes those settings, and requires Bukkit to accept the reload command. This is not runtime proof that arbitrary third-party CMI API or SQL writers are stopped; operators must quiesce all external CMI source writers during copy. A detected non-echo balance event invalidates the snapshot, blocks further migration permits, fails the checkpoint, and prevents completion. The partial target must not be activated and must be replaced by a fresh `-force` migration after source quiescence. CMI emits the event after authority mutation, so Syncmoney cannot veto arbitrary direct API calls. Runtime reload semantics and actual CMI migration remain NOT RUN. Unidentifiable non-echo balance events conservatively dirty the snapshot; outbound-suppressed echoes do not.

The E06 review also reproduced a synthetic completion receipt pairing an earlier write balance with a later observed cache version. `MemoryPendingStateTest.deferredRemoteBalanceWinsWhenCompletionReceiptCarriesItsVersion` failed before the fix and passed after `MemoryStateManager` began preferring a deferred remote snapshot on an equal version. Independent review confirms that this closes the observed E06 memory reconciliation race without adding a supported third-party API or storage contract. Exact balance/version receipt pairing for subsequent publish and SQL work remains with T05 and is not claimed fixed by T03.

Terminal retry ownership discovery: after maximum retries, `processFailedEvents` removes the event from its retry map without completing its reservation. The reservation and deferred account state remain retained, consuming one bounded global admission slot. This is fail-closed and can reduce admission capacity until restart/recovery or manual reconciliation. `OverflowLogInterface.log` does not report durable acknowledgment, and `RedisOverflowLog` may fall back to stderr; releasing accepted ownership without stronger evidence could lose the event. The current T03 disposition is to preserve ownership; no recovery/acknowledgment format or behavior was added.

NOT RUN: real Redis/SQL, actual CMI migration/runtime reload, LOCAL SQLite migration, restart/crash recovery, Folia/Canvas, and PlugDev E03/E06 scenarios. `:syncmoney-core:test` was not run because that module/scaffold does not exist; T03 used the existing root test source set to avoid expanding the bounded repair into a module split. T03 is COMPLETE for approved E03/E06 scope and the ADR-11 operational contract; no arbitrary external writer fence or live CMI result is claimed. T04 is COMPLETE and T05 is next under the dependency graph. The full root suite remains owner-routed, not a PASS.

Fingerprint fields are length-prefixed UTF-8, with an explicit null-UUID marker and a versioned format marker; balances use the existing two-decimal HALF_UP normalization. The digest omits fields that do not affect migration output. For single-source SQLite/MySQL readers, fingerprint and page queries share the same ordering keys. Multi-source candidates are canonicalized before merge because strategy ties otherwise depended on unspecified database row order.

NOT RUN for this follow-up: real/licensed CMI source runtime and migration, cross-database snapshot isolation, arbitrary third-party CMI API/SQL writer behavior during or after the fingerprint scan, live Redis/SQL, process crash/power-loss, Folia/Canvas, and PlugDev migration acceptance. The SHA fingerprint protects paused/resumed content only under ADR-11's operator quiescence precondition; it is not a live fence for external writers.

### T08 start / ADR-15 decision — 2026-10-08

- T07 is COMPLETE; T08 is IN PROGRESS on `linco/syncmoney-1.4.0-architecture-foundation-t00` at `76fc4c37d37bdf984118ee04373a76128c8520c8` before implementation.
- Source evidence: `OverflowLog.readAndClear()` clears the file after reading; `RedisOverflowLog.readAndClear()` deletes the Redis ZSET and silently drops JSON `balanceAfter`/`version` when converting to the legacy six-field format. Redis overflow also deletes old records after 24 hours or over 100,000 entries; fallback writes only to stderr. `EconomyEventConsumer` can retain a confirmed receipt in its in-memory retry map, but its shutdown drain currently does not durably checkpoint that state.
- ADR-15 ruling: add a separate internal checksummed `recovery-v1.jsonl` journal. Persist exact receipts for confirmed downstream retries, preserve NOT_SENT/REJECTED/ATTEMPTING distinctions, and never auto-replay an ambiguous legacy record. Keep `overflow.log` and the Redis legacy ZSET untouched during read; pending/ambiguous new-format records block rollback to 1.3.2. No public API, SQL schema, Redis protocol, or hard-crash/power-loss guarantee is added.
- Required tests/gates are still pending. T08 implementation must prove append/ack restart behavior, partial/corrupt preservation, disk/compaction failure retention, legacy SET ambiguity, queue-empty retry drain, and confirmed retry without a second Redis mutation. Raw test logs will be recorded here after execution.

Confirmed behavior: every Portal upload request is pinned to `https://central.sonatype.com/api/v1/publisher`, uses `publishingType=USER_MANAGED`, and refuses redirects. The input is copied once to a bounded private snapshot; signature verification, GAV/content hashing, ZIP inspection, and the upload all use those exact bytes. Upload intent and GAV/content hashes are written before the POST; an ambiguous upload result becomes `UPLOAD_UNKNOWN` and cannot be blindly retried. Invalid status shapes/types and status timeouts fail closed as `STATUS_UNKNOWN`; a later invocation resumes status polling without another upload. A changed content hash for the same GAV and a recorded `FAILED` deployment both stop before upload. `VALIDATED` does not imply public Maven Central availability and this client never publishes it.

NOT RUN: actual Central upload or authenticated staging resolution; namespace ownership proof; account-specific publisher tier/usage classification or eligibility; production signing credentials; Folia/Paper/Canvas runtime (not applicable to this publishing task); GitHub Actions execution. Account-level publication checks and any authorized public publish remain T23 gates. Next task by plan order: T19; its performance branch remains independent of T18.

### T19 queue membership and interruptible poll repair — 2026-10-10

- **Review finding and disposition.** A read-only concurrency review identified a window where LinkedBlockingQueue.poll had physically removed an event but queuedEvents still marked it queued. A concurrent complete/quarantine could therefore scan the remaining backlog. The barrier regression failed before linearization: it observed 2 backlog predicate inspections (expected 0), and completion did not wait for the dequeue transition. Fixed.
- **Interruption finding and disposition.** The first monitor-based implementation failed the pre-interrupted-poll regression because it could dequeue an available event without throwing InterruptedException. Replaced that draft with ReentrantLock.lockInterruptibly and a Condition. Poll checks interruption before the immediate dequeue, waits with awaitNanos, and returns the remaining timeout; signal/enqueue and dequeue/membership/removal transitions use the same lock. Poll releases this lock before taking commitGate.
- **Focused verification.** RED command for the race: .\gradlew.bat :syncmoney-bukkit:test --tests '*AdmissionReservationTest.completionCannotObserveHalfFinishedDequeueTransition' --rerun-tasks --no-daemon --console=plain; it failed with 2 inspected backlog events. RED command for the monitor draft: .\gradlew.bat :syncmoney-bukkit:test --tests '*AdmissionReservationTest.interruptedPollDoesNotDequeueAnAvailableEnvelope' --rerun-tasks --no-daemon --console=plain; the test failed. After the final lock/condition repair, the four focused cases (dequeue/completion barrier, pre-interrupted poll, queued identity completion, dequeued completion no-scan) passed with Gradle exit 0. The full Bukkit test suite subsequently passed.

### T19 paired t=2 performance review and scoped exception — 2026-10-11

- **Bound inputs.** Run `b5f5a11c-8467-4e30-b2d2-80b62d28b59d`; candidate `149e4ad96a42bdd2f7a46dcbb40fb194df6c011b`; baseline `71cc55dfeefe9a8f40a3835b051ddd324d353767`; source-tree SHA-256 `a8e1384928b12e6c62b7e38f07cc444aadd92873ee4fa0a90be897454f773848`. The 192-row JSON is 41,792,929 bytes, SHA-256 `8742140c6fb1b798c6f5f550a03829aed582c8475bdbe55c8eb856e8f4a99b76`, bound by `syncmoney-benchmarks/build/reports/benchmarks/transaction-paired-manifest-t2-b5f5a11c-8467-4e30-b2d2-80b62d28b59d.json`. JDK 25.0.4, JMH 1.37, SerialGC, 1 GiB, 2 producer threads, 5×1s warmup / 10×1s measurement / 3 forks. Independent review verified all expected rows, provenance, manifests, sample counts, per-trial postconditions and root-gate evidence; it found no Critical or correctness blocker.
- **B00 result.** On 48 matched operation/access-pattern/account-count cases: throughput was below 90% of baseline on 18/48; allocation exceeded 110% on 38/48; SampleTime p99 exceeded 110% on 42/48. Example `hot / 1 account / reject-withdraw`: throughput 0.0711 vs 11.6908 ops/µs (0.61%); allocation 5,025.22 vs 192.01 B/op (26.17×); SampleTime p99 21.18 vs 0.40 µs (52.95×). Worst recorded p99 example is `hot / 1,000 accounts / reject-withdraw`, 24.672 vs 0.400 µs (61.68×). The matrix does not suppress rejected cases; `TransactionBenchmarks` seeds a zero-balance control account and asserts the withdrawal rejects without accepted writes or balance/version/receipt mutation.
- **Source-supported cost analysis (not a per-step causal profile).** Candidate `TransactionWriter.withdrawAdmitted` acquires a migration `WriteLease`, validates readiness/version, executes the pre-transaction checks, obtains `MemoryStateManager.tryReserveWrite`, and then enters the account mutation path where insufficient funds are rechecked. `tryReserveWrite` takes a per-account lease and a bounded `EconomyWriteQueue` admission reservation; an insufficient withdrawal closes that unused reservation. In 1.3.2, the analogous writer checks the balance inside `stateManager.compute` and exits before constructing/enqueueing an `EconomyEvent`; it has no reserved-queue admission path on this rejection. Thus the candidate rejection path performs synchronization/admission/allocation work that does not end in a mutation. These gates protect memory/queue admission consistency, bounded backpressure, per-account mutation ordering and migration snapshot fencing. The measured report does not isolate the contribution of each gate or prove any one commit caused the full delta; the ratios are candidate-versus-1.3.2, not a before/after comparison of the T19 teardown fix.
- **Scope and limits.** This is a synthetic in-memory facade benchmark with a receipt adapter, not SQL/Redis throughput or a live Paper/Folia/Canvas run. JMH ran without captured fork CPU affinity; p99.9 intervals satisfy the configured sample minimum but do not establish cross-fork stationarity. The result is valid for its named profile only and must not be presented as production absolute capacity or as platform compatibility evidence.
- **Harness consumer asymmetry found during independent review.** For accepted events the current adapter calls `EconomyWriteQueue.complete/completePair`, exercising reserved-write completion bookkeeping and the current memory-state completion handler. The 1.3.2 adapter records a receipt and invokes `clearPendingTracking`; it does not execute the candidate-style reservation completion callback. The paired run remains a valid, hash-bound observation of these adapters, but it is not a like-for-like end-to-end consumer-cost comparison and cannot isolate writer-only latency. The `reject-withdraw` cases assert zero accepted events and do not enter either receipt-completion branch; the report still does not isolate their writer path from harness scheduling. Before assigning precise causal cost or changing architecture based on these deltas, add a bounded follow-up that aligns or explicitly separates consumer completion work. Do not discard this accepted matrix or alter its thresholds.
- **ADR-08 disposition under the user's delegated engineering authority.** ACCEPT the t=2 performance-threshold exception only to continue the required matched matrix and evaluate producerThreads=8. Keep the original 90% throughput / 110% allocation / 110% p99 thresholds unchanged; no rows are removed. All correctness, no-loss, bounded-admission, and prohibited-blocking gates remain hard blockers and are not waived. This is not a release performance approval: T19 remains IN_PROGRESS until t=8/report gates are recorded, and T22 must retain an explicit performance disposition. Reassess whether T20 is justified after t=8; do not claim measured PostgreSQL/Redis/real-server capacity from this JMH result.

**Task status:** T19 remains IN_PROGRESS. ### T19 row 037 validator false-positive correction (2026-10-11)

The first `Verify-T19-OpenLoop.ps1 -ExpectedCount 37` attempt stopped at row 037 with `counterConservation`. Report `redis-sql-open-loop-b348c203-a91b-44a0-ad93-ff560a123e4f-037.json` has SHA-256 `f1ed6c201598eb400a6ec1d5603c59a1c9a82572d4763b6f7343ed8149d1193d`, tuple `1|1|1`, and counters `offered=669820`, `accepted=601161`, `rejected=68659`, `persisted=601161`, `authorityRejected=0`. Thus offered equals accepted plus admission rejections, and accepted equals persisted. The checked-in runner source documents that `rejected` increments when the bounded load generator cannot acquire an in-flight permit (`maxInFlight=4096`) or cannot submit to its worker queue; `authorityRejected` is a separate Redis explicit-rejection counter after admission. The report records `queueMax=4096`, `valid=true`, `failureCategory=NONE`, and zero ambiguous, quarantine, money-invariant, and version-conflict counts. Its 669,820 response samples include local admission rejections; receipt and durable sample counts equal 601,161 accepted/persisted operations.

**Discovery / ruling:** local capacity rejection is an expected measured load-test outcome and is not a Redis authority rejection or money-correctness failure. The validator's equality `$rejected -eq $report.authorityRejected` was false. The ignored local validator was corrected to check the admission conservation equations and to require zero `authorityRejected` in the correctness gate, preserving the report's rejection-rate evidence. After the repair, `Verify-T19-OpenLoop.ps1 -ExpectedCount 37` passed with 37 unique tuples, the shared invocation ID `d2978cf2-9a34-4cc5-8725-57f6ceeccd58`, and summary SHA-256 `86a9fa391a0a3f15a45cd61508b41aba86b1a3613a816af88114a85423098832` (exit 0). This only clears the validator false positive; it does not establish matrix completion or a performance disposition.

## T21 player lifecycle review repair and evidence correction (2026-10-13)

**Findings and dispositions:** Two independent reviews found that the reusable runner could accept an event-bearing teleport without a successful `teleportAsync` future and that its server logout check matched only a reason prefix without binding the disconnect to `AcceptanceA`. The runner now requires exactly one successful future result and rejects missing, false, duplicate, malformed, or exceptional future evidence. Event-bearing paths still require a non-cancelled successful event sequence; eventless paths require entity-scheduler destination confirmation. Logout verification now binds to `AcceptanceA` and accepts only one matching expected-reason line whose full reason equals `T15 accepted-write logout scenario`; the normal `Disconnected` line from the earlier teleport is ignored. The assertion suite adds negative controls for all these cases and passes 14/14.

The six previously selected real-server reports and logs were preserved byte-for-byte. An offline correction audit applies the repaired predicates to the exact six historical report hashes, verifies all six server-log hashes, finds one successful teleport future and the exact expected `AcceptanceA` kick in each server log, and recomputes sizes and SHA-256 for all 24 stopped Redis data/AOF files. It also pins the original audit unchanged: `final-six-endpoint-audit-20261013.json`, SHA-256 `7f7718c69a8f2e2d37721fb752bad93e47e3a3b551e508f764c2f55d71cd6a37`. Correction audit: `build/reports/foundation/T21-player-scheduler/review-corrected-evidence-audit-20261013.json`, SHA-256 `a68237a9166d17fc94578bab6da38d9e39e4873e19c0a2136b20651d64f3d8cd`. The repaired runner was **NOT RUN** against new real-server sessions in this correction; the existing E2 server observations were independently checked against the stricter E1 predicates, and the old report artifacts remain the evidence source.

**Redis runtime provenance correction:** The original runner reused `$redisVersion` for the synthetic account's Redis version key, so each historical result incorrectly records `runtime.redis="4"`. The paired `redis.version=4` is the account version, not the server binary. Each selected Redis server log independently records version `8.10.1`. The runner now retains `$redisServerVersion` separately from `$accountVersion`; the historical JSON reports were not rewritten. The correction audit records each Redis log hash and the observed binary version.

The review also found that the acceptance probe read the teleport source world after calling `teleportAsync`, allowing a fast Folia/Canvas move to log the destination as the source. The probe now captures the source before the call. This diagnostic-only probe update rebuilt `SyncmoneyAcceptance.jar` to SHA-256 `fb83803013b1ec2a22b7295e42e41dc1c9290e8db0833969cc96324d5e182a64`; candidate plugin SHA-256 remained `55d42c2b72e86fdfd1d36e4f909e140f88256527a8e189c0c699d0cef89935d0`. The rebuilt probe was **NOT RUN** on a live endpoint after this logging-only change. Historical lifecycle acceptance uses the prior acceptance JAR and probe hash documented above; the source field was not an acceptance predicate.

## T21 Folia two-region cross-owner scheduler gate (2026-10-13)

**Historical evidence notice:** The initial reports listed in this section were produced before independent review corrections to the runner, verifier, and client completion predicate. **Historical result:** The initial two-player owner gate passed on both user-pinned Folia endpoints. The acceptance probe kept offline clients `AcceptanceA` and `AcceptanceB` connected, moved B to the Overworld at block `(16384, 16384)`, and ran an ownership observation on each player's entity scheduler. **Review discoveries and repair:** after the preceding PostgreSQL validator hardening, an independent review found the argv scan stopped before the final token, allowing an otherwise-valid command line followed by a dangling duplicate `-D` or `-p`. Both were reproduced as failing regressions: the legacy-loop run stopped at the dangling `-D` assertion (`t21-review-finding-red.log`, 3,322 bytes, SHA-256 `7b05b30a5ed23341914002f2b62ed5933ff6aa18e963634caa66945149900cd7`); the pre-operand-skip run stopped at the `-c`/`-D` assertion (`t21-review-option-operand-red.log`, 3,351 bytes, SHA-256 `06765d7412f643f35c4d3bb0423c77dfcdf72fd5d8e417846f49fb590ab292d6`). **Validator findings and repair:** Initial independent review found two false-accept cases. First, the offline predicate compared a report server hash only to the caller-supplied hash, so a caller and report that agreed on the wrong endpoint hash could pass; the predicate now checks the caller hash against the selected endpoint's hard-coded pin before comparing the report. Second, schema 1–3 logs are the historical Paper report format; the predicate now requires schema 4 `platformLogs` for Folia and Canvas while retaining schema 1–3 Paper compatibility. A follow-up review found that schema-4 metadata could still relabel a Folia report as Canvas because the retained stage logs were hashed but their startup identity was not parsed. The predicate now parses both schema-4 stage logs and requires each observed software/version/build to match the selected endpoint; missing, conflicting, or mismatched identities fail closed. The follow-up also found that the wrong-pin regression deleted its fixture logs before checking rejection; cleanup now occurs after that assertion, so the regression exercises the pin guard with otherwise valid retained logs. Regressions cover all four Folia/Canvas endpoint fixtures, a caller/report pair sharing the wrong Folia hash with intact logs, cross-platform relabeling, missing and conflicting log identities, and continued acceptance of legacy Paper schema-3 reports. The relabeling false-accept was reproduced before repair in `t21-review-platform-identity-red.log` (5,859 bytes; SHA-256 `80d23ea3982dd9edab85c629488452663dd3b10cbaa53276d995d4c017b4a79f`); the expected failure was `A schema-4 Canvas report with retained Folia startup logs was accepted.` The repaired focused suite passed 155/155. Targeted independent re-review confirmed schema 1–3 Paper compatibility and found no remaining findings. The validator/test/README changes do not alter Syncmoney runtime, API, config, SQL schema, Redis wire, or recovery-format contracts.

**Setup discovery and remaining scope:** The first MariaDB path resolution used a default `C:\Program Files\MariaDB 12.3\bin` path that is absent on this host. Prior successful local evidence identified `C:\Users\margo\scoop\apps\mariadb\current\bin`; the fresh runs used that local MariaDB `12.3.3` installation and passed. No services or runtime were started by the failed path-resolution attempt. The 12 new results close only the Folia/Canvas M05 `SYNC` SQL backend cells. Other runtime modes/resources, SQL-disabled/local paths, schema migration, fault injection, fleet-wide quiescence, broader scheduler cases, and the rest of T21 remain open or `NOT RUN`; licensed CMI runtime remains `BLOCKED / NOT RUN` because no authorized JAR is available. T21 remains `IN_PROGRESS`.

## T21 M04 ADR-15 shared-mode aggregate downgrade gate (2026-10-14)

**Result: PASS_BOUNDED_SUBCASE.** The M04 `LOCAL` SQLite cycle does not create the ADR-15 shared-mode spool by design: `EventConsumerManager` starts `LocalPersistenceWorker` and returns for `LOCAL`; the existing non-`LOCAL`, non-CMI path constructs `RecoverySpool`. The aggregate gate was therefore exercised through the existing M01–M03 SYNC upgrade/rollback runner, without changing M04's LOCAL runner or adding a recovery format.

The six M01–M03 reports listed in the T21 quiesced network-upgrade section cover the user-confirmed endpoints: Paper `1.21.6#48` / `26.3#166`, Folia `1.21.6#6` / `26.2#7`, and Canvas `1.21.8#603` / `26.3#972`. Each report retained SQL/Redis parity and the post-upgrade balances `1337.25/v2` and `765.50/v2`. In this turn, all six report files were rehashed against the recorded values and their status, candidate spool state, and four rollback observations were checked again; all matched. Supplemental Paper `26.3#178` remains outside the user-pinned range and is not used to expand this result.

The PostgreSQL validator requires the actual primary-key flag and exact eight-field catalog rows; MySQL retains its seven-field metadata predicate. New regressions reject an extra expression index in the lifecycle inventory and a candidate snapshot whose `syncmoney_audit_log_pkey` name is backed only by a unique index. ## T21 V05 initialization rollback and close-failure local lifecycle subcase (2026-10-14)

**Result: PASS_BOUNDED_E1 for the exercised local lifecycle contracts only.** No production source or product contract changed. Source inspection confirmed that `Syncmoney.onEnable()` catches initialization failures, invokes `onDisable()`, and then disables the plugin; `onDisable()` routes its owner steps through `ShutdownStepRunner`. `StorageManager.shutdown()` keeps SQL/Redis dependencies open while its database writer remains alive and closes them from the writer's `finally` path after the writer exits.

The final authoritative verification used JDK `25.0.4+7-LTS-189` and Gradle `9.8.0`: PowerShell command `$env:JAVA_HOME='C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-25.0.4'; & .\gradlew.bat ':syncmoney-bukkit:test' --rerun-tasks --no-daemon --console=plain --info` → `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, 18/18 actionable tasks; the test executor command also used `C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-25.0.4\bin\java.exe`. The final module output contains 109 JUnit XML files and 540 tests, with zero failures, errors, or skips. Log: `build/reports/foundation/T21-v05-initialization-close-failure/bukkit-module-tests-java25.log` (212,251 bytes; SHA-256 `bdac21017cbddd1659f320a2cea67030147bf6cb0625a3028ce5cd74faca96c1`). The three focused result XMLs in that final run report `PluginInitializationManagerTest` 2/2, `ShutdownStepRunnerTest` 1/1, and `StorageManagerShutdownTest` 1/1.

Observed assertions: the initialization helper attempts cleanup for the stage whose initialization threw, rolls back attempted stages in reverse order, and does not initialize later stages; close failure on one owner does not prevent other owners from closing. `ShutdownStepRunnerTest` injects an `AssertionError` and verifies later shutdown steps still run in order. `StorageManagerShutdownTest` holds a simulated JDBC writer beyond the close deadline, verifies SQL and Redis are not closed while it is alive, then releases it and verifies both dependencies close after writer exit.

Source SHA-256 pins: `PluginInitializationManagerTest.java` `3e815c23a5724f194d7218f037deec162e711592014effcbf7ff39badff15760`; `ShutdownStepRunnerTest.java` `5cd1ff5e9ff64b22983d65890ec68c706992afa784fa149acac4a6dfab8afe68`; `StorageManagerShutdownTest.java` `86ce10416801d92e3dff55ec85856eb958bae40fd560bc531f4ac71d4f0b7b39`; `Syncmoney.java` `48c561be89d44e3bc03aa6bc117af9b3ea516829e8c76f23f006bdb7f972a615`; `StorageManager.java` `a6f627ebc3da9639a51115611efb42831092f2ef0ac6d5059841e3c35e803381`; `PluginInitializationManager.java` `52671722e5802f465cae3dd02ee818c6df46ef0214a0ace210708d14e048c004`; `ShutdownStepRunner.java` `70fe3cf798fc780253d91e653d518059fed4cd1d17c632d52422e08e4f568b4b`.

**Evidence limits:** `PluginInitializationManager` is not used by the current production `Syncmoney.onEnable()` path; its tests establish that helper's isolated contract, not a live plugin startup rollback. ## T21 V03 newer audit schema startup-failure subcase (2026-10-14)

**Result: PASS_BOUNDED_SUBCASE (E2) for PostgreSQL 18.1 on minimum Paper only.** On Paper `1.21.6#48` (server JAR SHA-256 `35e2dfa66b3491b9d2f0bb033679fa5aca1e1fdf097e7a06a80ce8afeda5c214`), Java `25.0.4+7-LTS-189`, Redis `8.10.1` DB 15, Syncmoney `1.4.0-alpha.1` (JAR SHA-256 `57b717e7704e93d6086341c08d4a34e53a74efc0e9c44877a3e856e0db90c662`), PostgreSQL rejected the seeded audit schema version 12 because this candidate supports version 11. The plugin did not complete startup, logged initialized-owner rollback and INFO-level Hikari shutdown, then Paper exited normally with code 0. The run-owned PostgreSQL/Redis shutdowns exited normally without forced stop; SQL connections, Redis clients, and Redis DB 15 keys were zero after rollback.

Runtime report: `build/reports/foundation/T21-sql-runtime/postgresql-sync-minimum-paper-20261014-182145-5c4a96973f3e4cbb80c60c932325f223/result.json`, SHA-256 `680c25865d30a6114bd988ec97ddaf4b8fdb68246130262e6f6fbcf9eb3d4257`. The pre-start fixture had audit version row 12, a 16-column `syncmoney_audit_log` table with all 44 `information_schema.columns` metadata fields, four indexes, and one sentinel row. Those four audit-state snapshots are byte-for-byte equal before and after candidate startup; the report records PostgreSQL `shutdownTargetVerified=true`. Independent evidence review matched the report hash, retained log hashes/byte counts, candidate/server/artifact pins, five source pins, PlugDev commit/CLI hash, normal process exits, and cleanup observations, and found no discrepancy.

Runtime provenance: Acceptance JAR SHA-256 `dd1e85271269b8dfa4799d2341778238e85b0af346043fd386143b2b3705a68e`; API consumer SHA-256 `b35f098f969387153f1feca27f1ea2535d522a859a69974a5d9d6960ab50169d`; local PlugDev source commit `b59871ae8d9f2731d2bcbca061a735edddd23eb2`, CLI SHA-256 `3a600872a3c95bb67b960bdb5efcbb84eb675110f89146566bedb1835ad047d7`. Report source pins: runner `9ff9ba74ac9624c692ad66acfcd42b94b5f3da5abad4ade53d4869af293abf66`; pre-repair startup validator/test `055f9efc06909405bb046121ac9cc3965074b8bca7665563f21ba2f34fa3594c` / `6389eaa73abb98e2cf7b41e01b6fa06aed99e619fb3b4fb4617f8c662226fc28`; shared validator/test `bf12a605d6f1d172d02bfdbe216274d4709276b4a5aec362f44aca33b2e5bdba` / `ab6eca1ceb355ca0b464bed0dd668c6dbfc3d4951f1065b069d8420a8c126f5b`.

**Discovery and claim boundary:** the database initially had no main schema or `players` table. Startup created main schema version row `1` and an empty `players` table before detecting the newer audit schema and rejecting plugin startup. Thus this case demonstrates preservation of the pre-existing audit schema and resource rollback, not an atomic rollback of every SQL schema change. It does not cover MySQL/MariaDB, other Paper/Folia/Canvas builds, other modes/resources, or other startup failure points.

**Validator review repair:** an independent validator review reproduced that changing the PostgreSQL shutdown's `shutdownTargetVerified` from `true` to `false` still let the report predicate pass when `cleanupFailures` was empty. The producer already records the field and reports cleanup failure when it is false, but the predicate did not independently require the recorded Boolean. The predicate now requires actual Boolean `true`, and a negative fixture rejects the former counterexample. RED was observed before the fix; after the fix the focused test passed 15/15. Targeted independent re-review confirmed the report now requires `true`, found no new gap, and passed the same 15/15 fixture suite. The runtime report is source-pinned to the pre-repair validator (`055f9efc06909405bb046121ac9cc3965074b8bca7665563f21ba2f34fa3594c`) and test (`6389eaa73abb98e2cf7b41e01b6fa06aed99e619fb3b4fb4617f8c662226fc28`); the post-review validator/test hashes are `10eeda4f0e75517934798f0f094a22185c99a36b52c3e4f591e222134fb9eed9` and `75689460b76a737cd004c2c2192f024311bc18be8bd2ceea96c68864204f5032`. Treat the runtime execution and post-review local predicate test as separate evidence; the E2 report was not rerun with the tightened validator.

Review reconciliation: an earlier startup-scope review snapshot flagged Redis/exit field and platform log path mismatches plus a missing INFO-level check. Those findings are superseded by the final runner, validator, fixture, and retained report: Redis is validated by its emitted version/PID/ownership fields; `processExitCodeObserved` / `processExited` and `candidate-startup-failure` / `logs\platform-candidate-startup-failure.txt` agree across producer and predicate; and the predicate requires the INFO-level Hikari line, with a WARN-only mutation rejected by the fixture. An independent code review found two false-positive paths in the previous success predicate: it accepted column names without checking SQL metadata, and it accepted a non-unique PostgreSQL index named as the primary key. Replaying the old predicate against wrong-type `sequence` and non-unique primary-index fixtures reproduced both false accepts. The repaired predicate checks the complete ordered v10/v11 column sets, dialect-specific SQL type/length/precision, nullability, default semantics, table/database identity, generation metadata, and exact index shape; PostgreSQL's primary index must be unique. New regressions reject an integer `sequence`, short `request_id`, wrong sequence default or JSON value type, wrong nullability, and non-unique PostgreSQL primary index. The numeric JSON default fixture exposed a coercion false accept during repair; the final validator requires the observed default to be a string.

## T21 M04 no-receipt fixture provenance discovery and repair (2026-10-16)

**Finding:** review of `t21-local-persistence-journal.ps1` found that it unconditionally added `transactions.request_id` and `idx_transactions_request_id` before branching on `ReceiptState`. Therefore, the minimum/maximum-Paper no-receipt reports proved the request-ID receipt was absent before journal replay, but they did not prove candidate startup performed the additive migration from the historical 1.3.2 schema. The test-first regression reproduced the defect: `t21-local-persistence-journal.test.ps1` failed at its explicit pre-start schema assertion. This is a harness/claim-evidence gap; no product-code defect was established by this finding.

**Repair:** schema setup now runs only for the committed-receipt seed. The absent-receipt fixture and retained pre-replay SQLite snapshot keep both request-ID column and index absent; the seed report captures those counts and the auditor independently checks them. The runtime runner inspects the schema after the candidate is enabled and before the first replay balance read, records the observation, and requires both schema objects. The offline auditor checks the report observation and final SQLite state. Source-pin validation remains strict; old predicate-normalization fallbacks do not make reports auditable when their full runner/auditor/helper source pins cannot be reproduced. A regression verifies stale source pins are rejected.

**Focused local verification at the time of repair:** `t21-local-persistence-journal.test.ps1`, `t21-upgrade-cycle-audit-contract.test.ps1`, `t21-upgrade-validation.test.ps1`, `run-upgrade-cycle.test.ps1`, and `t21-audit-schema-upgrade-validation.test.ps1` all passed. The PowerShell parser passed for 16 T21/runner scripts with zero errors. The earlier `t21-upgrade-validation.test.ps1` attempt failed because it asserted the old absent-receipt audit expression; its source contract was updated to require the repaired independent schema checks and strict source-pin predicate, and the repeat passed. At this historical checkpoint, runtime verification was pending; the six accepted E2 reports and refreshed audits are recorded below. Java/Gradle product tests are **NOT RUN** because only PlugDev harness/tests and planning evidence changed.

## T21 M01–M03 audit-enabled supplemental current-stable Paper `26.3#194` upgrade and rollback (2026-10-16)

**Result: `PASS_BOUNDED_QUIESCED_UPGRADE (E2)` for one supplemental case.** The isolated run exercised a two-node SYNC sequence on Paper `26.3#194`, Java `25.0.4+7-LTS-189`, PostgreSQL `18.1`, and Redis `8.10.1` DB 15. It started both nodes on Syncmoney `1.3.2`, seeded accounts at `1000.00/v1` and `520.00/v1`, stopped and drain-verified them before taking the pre-upgrade backup, upgraded node A and then node B to candidate `1.4.0-alpha.1`, and normally rolled both nodes back to `1.3.2`. SQL audit and Redis hybrid audit were enabled; cleanup/export workers were disabled.

The two candidate writes reached `1337.25/v2` and `765.50/v2`. All six lifecycle snapshots show those SQL balances/versions matching Redis after candidate drains and after rollback; the two baseline snapshots retain the seeded values. Main and audit schema-version rows remained `1|1` and `audit|11`. SQL audit counts for both disposable accounts increased from one to two after candidate writes and remained at two after rollback. Both candidate shutdowns recorded drained economy, database, SQL audit, and Redis hybrid-audit owners with zero queued/buffered, in-flight, retry, stale, dead-letter, dropped, and late-rejected counts. The node A recovery journal had six valid frames (four records, two acknowledgements), zero pending work, and the same SHA-256 through rollback; node B had no journal before or after rollback. All six normal stops and process exits, all four backend shutdown observations, both node cleanups, and zero run-owned Gradle daemons were verified; the report records no runtime or cleanup failure.

The quiescence evidence is bounded to two synthetic Paper nodes and the acceptance probe: both nodes were normally stopped before backup, and the harness issued no producer calls between maintenance start and candidate acceptance probes. This does not prove production fleet-wide quiescence or cover external producers outside the harness.

## T21 V03 PostgreSQL player-row timestamp precision revalidation (2026-10-16)

**Discovery and repair:** the preceding 18-cell matrix established bounded one-row preservation, but its PostgreSQL snapshot rendered updated_at with YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS, discarding PostgreSQL timestamp fractional seconds. A change confined to one microsecond could therefore pass the JSON equality predicate. The runner now formats PostgreSQL timestamps with YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS.US; the sentinel validator expects six fractional digits for PostgreSQL, and regression tests reject a .000001 mutation against the .000000 fixture. The historical MySQL-MinimumPaper task-label alias is constrained to MySQL / minimum Paper; cross-product and wrong-endpoint cases are rejected. These are PlugDev harness/validator changes; product Java sources were not changed.

The six MySQL and six MariaDB E2 reports remain the earlier bounded observations with their original source pins; they were not rerun or recharacterized as having used the current PostgreSQL precision validator.

## T21 Folia cross-owner exact client completion marker (2026-10-16)

**Discovery and repair:** an independent review found that both the Mineflayer listener and shared assertion helper used substring matching for `T21_CROSS_OWNER_PASS player=<username>`. A prefixed message, a suffixed message, or the near-name `AcceptanceAA` could therefore be accepted as a successful completion for `AcceptanceA`. Both checks now require exact whole-line equality. The regression cases assert that these invalid messages return false and leave the already-passed set unchanged.

**RED/GREEN evidence:** before the predicate repair, `node --test tools/plugdev/player-scheduler-lifecycle-assertions.test.mjs` produced 25 passes and one failure by accepting an invalid marker. ## T21 M04 LOCAL SQLite graceful shutdown-timeout handoff and replay — minimum Paper (2026-10-17)

**Result: `PASS_BOUNDED_SUBCASE` (E2).** This fresh minimum-Paper rerun corrects and supersedes the earlier `paper-1.21.6-48-20261017-072033-5e559be7593f48f796c6219c9c9589e6` report (SHA-256 `f4b11e22c27aef2b2eed8a9eaa99fb787aea249085974fb3133aa6d2bfb57754`): its snapshot labelled `recovery-1.4-before-first-balance-read` was collected after the first balance-read command. The runner now captures SQLite balances, request receipts, and journal size immediately after startup recovery/schema observation and before issuing that read; a regression pins this order. The old report remains retained but is excluded from acceptance.

The accepted run used Java `25.0.4+7-LTS-189`, Paper `1.21.6#48` (SHA-256 `35e2dfa66b3491b9d2f0bb033679fa5aca1e1fdf097e7a06a80ce8afeda5c214`), candidate Syncmoney `1.4.0-alpha.1` (SHA-256 `57b717e7704e93d6086341c08d4a34e53a74efc0e9c44877a3e856e0db90c662`, source checkout `777da48739a0598009fbb9d649d2a37a332d29d1`), baseline `1.3.2` (SHA-256 `442a404276b538ce807b0f063fb37920be85e60961a52a475b3f3524d08f4f10`, source `71cc55dfeefe9a8f40a3835b051ddd324d353767`), and local PlugDev `b59871ae8d9f2731d2bcbca061a735edddd23eb2`. The profile was LOCAL SQLite, guard-on, Redis/shared SQL/optional modules off.

During the candidate graceful RCON stop, an independently held SQLite WAL writer lock kept two accepted writes pending. The stop command exited 0; observed stop duration was 13,149 ms against the 10,000 ms drain deadline; both timeout and durable-handoff markers were present; the Java process exit was verified and forced cleanup was false. The lock release and subsequent SQLite writer probe succeeded. Before replay, the SQLite snapshot still held `100.00/v7` and `0.00/v3`, transaction count 1, and zero receipts for both accepted request IDs. The copied checksummed journal contained two records (498 bytes; SHA-256 `5cc74c576192a753813958dc34c63b90a5c78432a40947c6967ee743bf655b47`). On the next 1.4 startup, the runtime log reports recovery of two accepted writes at `07:30:38`, then successful plugin enable at `07:30:38`; the first balance read is logged at `07:30:46`. The now-correct pre-read snapshot contains `1337.25/v9` and `765.50/v5`, exactly one receipt per accepted request (two total), transaction count 3, and a zero-byte journal. Candidate normal shutdown and the 1.3.2 rollback read both completed with expected balances.

## T21 V03 successful v10-to-v11 migration with existing player-row preservation — minimum and maximum Paper / PostgreSQL (2026-10-17)

**Result: `PASS_BOUNDED_SUBCASE (E2)` for minimum and maximum Paper / PostgreSQL.** This extends the successful-migration player-row case from four Paper/MySQL-or-MariaDB cells to six Paper/backend cells by adding PostgreSQL `18.1` on the two exact user-pinned Paper endpoints. It does not expand the formal platform bounds: minimum Paper `1.21.6#48`, maximum Paper `26.3#166`, minimum/maximum Folia `1.21.6#6` / `26.2#7`, and minimum/maximum Canvas `1.21.8#603` / `26.3#972`.

**Ruling and discovery:** Enable only the existing-player-row PostgreSQL case on minimum/maximum Paper, keeping all CurrentStable, Folia, Canvas, unsupported-product, and unpinned endpoint controls rejected. The regression first reproduced RED at `PostgreSQL/Minimum`. Inspection found the successful-migration fixture used MySQL-only `ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` and inline-index syntax; the PostgreSQL fixture now uses PostgreSQL-compatible `TIMESTAMP` DDL and a separate `CREATE INDEX`, matching the established isolated PostgreSQL player-row fixture for the failure-path case. This is fixture/harness coverage only; no product schema, engine, recovery format, wire, or public contract changed. Cost if this ruling is wrong: the test may preserve an isolated fixture whose PostgreSQL `players` DDL differs from an operator's legacy table, so this remains one-row runtime evidence rather than a general schema-compatibility claim.

**Confirmed behavior:** On both endpoints, the candidate preserved main schema version `1`, migrated audit schema `10→11`, expanded the audit table from 13 to 15 columns, and retained all four required PostgreSQL audit indexes. The pre-existing SQL `players` row remained one row and JSON-identical before/after: UUID `00000000-0000-0000-0000-00000000cafe`, name `T21-ROW-SENTINEL`, balance `1234.56`, version `73`, server marker `t21-player-preservation`, and timestamp `2026-10-16 12:34:56.000000`. Paper, PostgreSQL, and Redis each exited with code `0`; shutdown was not forced and cleanup failures were zero. Both runs used Java `25.0.4+7-LTS-189`, PostgreSQL `18.1`, Redis `8.10.1` DB 15, candidate `1.4.0-alpha.1` SHA-256 `57b717e7704e93d6086341c08d4a34e53a74efc0e9c44877a3e856e0db90c662`, and local PlugDev commit `b59871ae8d9f2731d2bcbca061a735edddd23eb2`.

## T21 V03 successful audit-schema migration with multiple existing player rows (2026-10-17)

**Result: PASS_BOUNDED_SUBCASE (E2), 2026-10-17.** Current-source runtime evidence covers three seeded `players` rows on the 18 endpoint × SQL-product cells pinned at the time. It extends the earlier one-row-only limit for this successful-migration subcase on those historical endpoints; it does not establish current-maximum multi-row coverage, a complete database inventory, or whole-database atomic rollback.

**Selected scope:** Add a separate opt-in PlugDev case that seeds three distinct `players` rows, including the existing sentinel plus two records with different UUIDs, names, balances, versions, servers, and timestamps. Canonicalize captured row JSON by UUID so MySQL/MariaDB aggregate ordering cannot create false differences. Require row count `3` and the exact fixture contents both before and after successful v10→v11 migration, while retaining main schema v1, advancing audit schema v10→v11, preserving the audit sentinel and v11 metadata, and verifying the same pinned artifact and clean shutdown predicate. Keep the existing one-row scenario and historical evidence unchanged.

**Acceptance gates used for this historical run:** RED/GREEN focused PowerShell regressions for row-set validation, missing/changed/extra rows, array-order normalization, task identity, and the six then-pinned endpoint selectors; current-source PlugDev tests and PowerShell parsing; three SQL products across Paper `1.21.6#48` / `26.3#166`, Folia `1.21.6#6` / `26.2#7`, and Canvas `1.21.8#603` / `26.3#972` (18 historical cells); per-report offline audits plus an independent manifest/report/artifact/log verifier; read-only review; and `git diff --check`. Java/product tests are required only if product code changes. This is bounded preservation evidence for the seeded three rows on the earlier endpoints, not current-maximum coverage, a complete database inventory, or a whole-database atomic-rollback claim.

**Observed behavior and bounds:** The current-source opt-in runs completed normal audit-schema v10→v11 migration on every cell. All three seeded rows were byte-for-byte identical in the canonical UUID-sorted snapshots before and after migration; row count remained `3`, main schema remained v1, audit sentinel and v11 metadata remained present, and platform/backend cleanup reported no failure. PostgreSQL snapshots retain the dialect's `.000000` timestamp precision. The fixtures contain only three known rows; they do not prove that every database row was inventoried or that all schema changes roll back atomically.

## T21 outer `Syncmoney.onEnable()` initialization rollback (2026-10-17)

**Result: `PASS_BOUNDED_E1` for the outer plugin initialization-failure path.** `SyncmoneyInitializationRollbackTest` executes the production `Syncmoney.onEnable()` and `onDisable()` methods on a real-method Mockito instance. It injects an `EconomyServiceManager.initialize()` failure after `StorageManager.initialize()` has run and both owner fields are assigned. Both owners then throw during shutdown; the test verifies Economy closes before Storage (reverse of those two construction steps), Storage is still attempted, and Bukkit's `PluginManager.disablePlugin()` is called only after both close attempts. A second `onDisable()` invocation leaves the Storage shutdown count at one. No production source changed; the existing outer catch/rollback behavior met this bounded contract.

The fixture constructor-mocks `SyncmoneyConfig`, `ConfigMerger`, `MessageService`, `StorageManager`, and `EconomyServiceManager` to prevent filesystem, SQL, Redis, scheduler, or other Bukkit startup effects. The test therefore verifies production lifecycle wiring and shutdown ordering at the injected boundary, not those owners' actual initialization or resource cleanup. Mockito bypasses JavaPlugin construction, so the test initializes the private shutdown guard reflectively. No Paper, Folia, or Canvas startup runtime was run for this case.

| Check | Command / observed result | Retained evidence |

## T21 §21 startup rollback owner-graph follow-up (2026-10-17)

**Result: `PASS_BOUNDED_E1` for the outer initialization-failure rollback path and the active SyncManager version-check barrier.** The startup-failure path now quiesces the economy write owner and stops inbound/scheduled sync producers before draining. `SyncManager.stopInboundProducers()` waits for an already-running version check to finish. Rollback then attempts assigned owner cleanup in reverse construction order: plugin context, web services, owned EventBus listeners, permissions, commands, event consumers, audit, listeners, baltop, breaker, sync, economy, and storage. Each step is isolated so injected cleanup exceptions do not prevent later owners from being attempted. Normal `onDisable()` keeps its documented dependency-aware order. EventBus cleanup is guarded by plugin-instance ownership.

`SyncmoneyInitializationRollbackTest` injects `CommandServiceManager.initialize()` failure after all owners created by this LOCAL fixture are assigned, makes cleanup methods throw, verifies the pre-drain sequence and reverse cleanup continuation, and confirms a later `onDisable()` does not repeat owner cleanup or economy quiescence. `SyncManagerLifecycleTest` uses latches to hold a Redis snapshot read while shutdown starts; it verifies the stop path remains waiting until the read is released, then completes. The test read waits solely on its explicit release latch, released in `finally`, so test-thread scheduling does not race a competing timeout. `SyncmoneyEventBusTest` covers both preserving a foreign owner and clearing the actual owner; its fixture resets the singleton around each test.

## T21 V03 newer audit-schema v12 rejection — historical earlier endpoint matrix (2026-10-17)

**Result: `PASS_BOUNDED_SUBCASE (E2)` across the 18 endpoint × SQL-product cells pinned at the time.** The candidate supports audit schema v11 and rejected the seeded v12 audit schema on Paper `1.21.6#48` / `26.3#166`, Folia `1.21.6#6` / `26.2#7`, and Canvas `1.21.8#603` / `26.3#972`, using MySQL `8.0.42`, MariaDB `12.3.3-MariaDB`, and PostgreSQL `18.1`. These reports cover the earlier user-pinned endpoints and do not satisfy the updated current-maximum v12-rejection gates; no supplemental endpoint was included. Every cell used Java `25.0.4+7-LTS-189`, candidate `1.4.0-alpha.1` SHA-256 `ccda31eeee545e6266d05af917dcda3f4e6603f5a7c51d1bc26a040a53161789`, Redis `8.10.1` DB 15, and the local PlugDev source commit `b59871ae8d9f2731d2bcbca061a735edddd23eb2` (CLI SHA-256 `3a600872a3c95bb67b960bdb5efcbb84eb675110f89146566bedb1835ad047d7`; complete CLI distribution manifest SHA-256 `f57b296b2e4de10dec9dd7a83a51f3e0f95fb5ef27d5de2934e9b4ef56e0fc16`). The PlugDev checkout remained clean and its source/CLI pins did not change during the matrix.

**Decision and discovery:** Current Paper runtime logs show the startup rollback marker, INFO-level Syncmoney Hikari pool shutdown completion, and then Bukkit's `Disabling Syncmoney v1.4.0-alpha.1` marker in that order. The rollback has already set the once-only shutdown guard, so `onDisable()` returns without emitting the legacy `Syncmoney disabled.` message. A prior v12 run on the short SSD report root correctly observed candidate rejection and pool shutdown, but the runner timed out waiting for the obsolete message and forced platform cleanup; that run is `FAIL` and excluded. A preceding long report-root attempt failed before Paper startup during MySQL datadir initialization and is also excluded as a fixture/path failure. No product code or public/configuration/SQL/Redis contract changed for this subcase. The runner and strict report validator now require the ordered rollback → INFO pool shutdown → Bukkit disable markers, and the runner still checks normal platform shutdown. A regression fixture was first run against the old predicate and failed, then passed after the harness change; the validator also rejects missing Bukkit disable evidence.

**Confirmed behavior and limits:** For every accepted report, startup rejected audit schema version 12 because the candidate supports version 11. The audit version row, all 16 audit columns, all four indexes, and the sentinel row were unchanged. Startup had already created main schema v1 and an empty `players` table before rejecting the audit schema, so this establishes preservation of the seeded audit state, not atomic rollback of every schema change or the whole database. All 18 candidate platform processes and their SQL/Redis backends exited normally without forced cleanup; strict audits found zero cleanup failures, residual SQL connections, Redis clients, or Redis DB 15 keys.

## T21 Paper network runner cleanup hardening before first cell (2026-10-19)

**Gate state: `IN_PROGRESS`; no Paper network endpoint cell is accepted.** The minimum Paper `1.21.6#48` still has four preserved attempts, all excluded from acceptance as recorded above. This repair addresses run-owned PostgreSQL cleanup after an attempted restore; it does not change the acceptance result of those attempts.

**Repair:** Independent review identified two P2 defects in `tools/plugdev/t21-paper-network-runner.mjs`: a PostgreSQL instance started during cleanup could survive a readiness timeout because the final stop was skipped, and `stopPostgres` treated any nonzero `pg_ctl status` code as proof the service was stopped. ## T21/V03 minimum-Paper MySQL DatabaseManager initial-schema permission-denial feasibility — BLOCKED before runtime (2026-10-19)

**Result: BLOCKED / NOT VERIFIED.** The selected cell is minimum Paper 1.21.6#48 / MySQL 8.0.42. This is a pre-runtime feasibility result, not a runtime failure or acceptance.

syncmoney-bukkit/src/main/java/noietime/syncmoney/storage/db/DatabaseManager.java calls createDatabaseIfNotExists() in its constructor before configuring and constructing the main Syncmoney-HikariCP pool. The MySQL ensure branch connects with the configured application account and runs CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS. It uses a temporary Syncmoney-TempDB datasource for this operation; the main pool is constructed only after the ensure method returns. The PlugDev fixture creates the isolated database as root and grants the application role only SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE. MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual §15.1.12 requires CREATE for CREATE DATABASE [IF NOT EXISTS]; §8.2.2 describes that same privilege as enabling creation of new databases and tables. Under this selected grant set, the ensure statement is expected to fail before the main pool and target CREATE TABLE players denial. Granting CREATE to reach the target table statement also grants the privilege used by that statement. This is an inference from implementation and official documentation, not a live observation of MySQL 8.0.42.

## T21/V03 MySQL blocker disposition, MariaDB feasibility, and next gate (2026-10-19)

The maintainer selected the recommended disposition: preserve minimum-Paper `1.21.6#48` / MySQL `8.0.42` as `BLOCKED / NOT VERIFIED` and authorize the next dependency-ready gate. This decision does not revise the acceptance to the separate pre-main-pool database-creation error and does not authorize a database-provisioning/product-contract change. The MySQL case remains pre-runtime; no MySQL process was accessed or changed.

The adjacent minimum-Paper/MariaDB `12.3.3-MariaDB` initial-schema denial was checked before runtime. `DatabaseManager` routes MariaDB-compatible `databaseType=mysql` through `createDatabaseIfNotExists()` before constructing the main Hikari pool. MariaDB's `CREATE DATABASE` documentation requires the CREATE privilege; its GRANT documentation says database-scoped CREATE may be granted on a database that does not yet exist and also grants CREATE on all tables in that database. Under the planned isolated fixture, a DML-only account cannot pass the ensure statement; granting database-scoped CREATE would also allow the target table creation. This is a source/documentation feasibility inference, not live MariaDB evidence. The current bounded-case validator also intentionally does not select MariaDB. No MariaDB service or runtime was started; this dialect remains `BLOCKED / NOT VERIFIED` for this specific post-pool denial criterion.

Official references: [MariaDB CREATE DATABASE](https://mariadb.com/docs/server/reference/sql-statements/data-definition/create/create-database) and [MariaDB GRANT — database privileges](https://mariadb.com/docs/server/reference/sql-statements/account-management-sql-statements/grant#database-privileges). The page text states CREATE is required and that database-scoped CREATE grants CREATE on all tables.

**Next selected dependency-ready gate:** minimum supported Folia `1.21.6#6` / PostgreSQL `18.1` for the same bounded DatabaseManager initial-schema failure and cleanup behavior. Paper minimum and current-maximum PostgreSQL cases are already accepted; the Folia case extends runtime-platform evidence and does not alter the MySQL/MariaDB acceptance or make a general Folia-safety claim.

At this pre-runtime checkpoint, validator/runner/auditor work was complete and runtime was **NOT RUN** pending listener/process preflight. The later isolated execution and report-specific audit are recorded below. Independent read-only review found 0 Critical, 0 Important, and one non-blocking Minor recommendation; details and scope limits are recorded in the review row and retained note below. New server JAR pins use `serverJarSha256`; the auditor retains a Paper-only fallback for existing reports that predate that neutral field. Regression coverage rejects the wrong Folia platform and preserves the MySQL/MariaDB fail-fast boundary.
